translationRepairs: At the end of Zhenguang, Minister of Works Li Chong was made regional commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as his chief clerk.
At the end of Zhenguang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong was made regional commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as his chief clerk.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. Chinese 尚書令 is Director/Prefect of the Masters of Writing, not Minister of Works (司空).
At the end of Zhenguang, Minister of Works Li Chong was made Regional Commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as chief clerk.
At the end of Zhenguang, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Li Chong was made Regional Commander of the commandery and led forces against the Rouran, with Langen as chief clerk.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. Chinese 尚書令 is mistranslated as Minister of Works.
Chong reported it up to Qin; the matter rested without response.
Chong reported it upward in a memorial; the matter rested without response.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 秦聞 is a corruption/misreading of 奏聞 'report upward'; Qin is not a place or addressee here.
At the time Wang Daoxi, attendant respondant to edicts, enjoyed Zhuang's trust. Langen attached himself to him, seeking merit in the field.
At the time Wang Daoxi, attendant respondent to edicts, enjoyed Zhuang's trust. Langen attached himself to him, seeking merit in the field.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. English typo: respondant should be respondent.
At the time, Attendant Respondant to Edicts Wang Daoxi enjoyed Zhuang's trust; Langen attached himself to him, seeking to win merit abroad.
At the time, Attendant Respondent to Edicts Wang Daoxi enjoyed Zhuang's trust; Langen attached himself to him, seeking to win merit abroad.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. English typo: Respondant should be Respondent.
Gao Huan, with no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Wucheng.
Gao Huan, with no choice, thereupon enthroned Emperor Xiaowu.
The ruler enthroned by Gao Huan here is conventionally called Emperor Xiaowu in English, not Emperor Wucheng or the ambiguous Emperor Wu.
The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet because Langen and others framed and defamed him, he was deeply censured by contemporary opinion.
The deposed emperor had long possessed virtue and achievement, yet because Langen and others framed and defamed him, they were deeply censured by contemporary opinion.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. Subject of 深為時論所非 is Langen and the others who framed him, not the deposed emperor.
At the beginning of Taichang he was made equal in protocol to three imperators, soon additionally opener of a government office, and enfeoffed marquis of Julu County with seven hundred households.
At the beginning of Taichang he was made equal in protocol to the Three Dukes, soon additionally opener of a government office, and enfeoffed marquis of Julu County with seven hundred households.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 三司 denotes the Three Dukes; “three imperators” is a clear mistranslation.

At the beginning of Taichang he was made Equal in Protocol to Three Imperators, soon additionally Opener of a Government Office, enfeoffed Marquis of Julu County with a fief of seven hundred households.

At the beginning of Taichang he was made Equal in Protocol to the Three Dukes, soon additionally Opener of a Government Office, enfeoffed Marquis of Julu County with a fief of seven hundred households.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 三司 denotes the Three Dukes; “Three Imperators” is a clear mistranslation.
Emperor Wucheng severely condemned him. Langen, terrified, cited illness and resigned as vice director.
Emperor Xiaowu severely condemned him. Langen, terrified, cited illness and resigned as Vice Director.
The same 武帝 reference is Emperor Xiaowu; the revised sentence also regularizes the office title.
Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Yin provinces, inspector of Ding Province, duke over the masses, and palace attendant, with the posthumous title Wenzuan.
Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in Ji, Ding, and Yin provinces, inspector of Ding Province, duke over the masses, and palace attendant, with the posthumous title Wenxuan.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 文宣 is Wenxuan, not Wenzuan.
Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Yin, Inspector of Ding Province, Duke over the Masses, Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Wenzuan.
Posthumously granted supervisor of military affairs in the three provinces of Ji, Ding, and Yin, Inspector of Ding Province, Duke over the Masses, Palace Attendant, with posthumous title Wenxuan.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 文宣 is Wenxuan, not Wenzuan.
At the beginning of Wuping he served as palace investigating censor, then was transferred to secretariat attendant and awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall.
At the beginning of Wuping he served as palace investigating censor, then was transferred to secretariat attendant and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 文林館 is Wenlin Hall, not Wulin Hall.
At the beginning of Wuping he was palace investigating censor; he was transferred to attendant of the Secretariat and awaited edicts at the Wulin Hall.
At the beginning of Wuping he was palace investigating censor; he was transferred to attendant of the Secretariat and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 文林館 is Wenlin Hall, not Wulin Hall.
Soon he was removed and made attendant of the Yellow Gate; he was transferred to general and right grand master for splendid happiness.
Soon he was appointed Gentleman Attendant at the Yellow Gate, then promoted to General and Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
除 means appointment here, and the revised wording renders both offices in grammatical English.
Soon he was removed and made governor of Xu Province; he was given three hundred retainers of Guangzong and a thousand retainers of Qinghe.
Soon he was appointed Inspector of Xu Province; he was given three hundred retainers from Guangzong and one thousand from Qinghe.
除 means appointment, while 刺史 and the two 部曲 allotments are clearer as Inspector and retainers.
Ling was by nature arrogant and overbearing; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, taking and accepting as she pleased — government and customs were not established.

Ling was by nature arrogant and overbearing; he favored his concubine Lady Feng and lent her his punitive authority, so she extorted and accepted bribes at will — government and customs were not established.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 恣情取受 is Lady Feng's conduct under borrowed authority; the literal leaves the subject ambiguous and omits the extortion sense.

When Shou went on a mission to hire Liang and passed through Xu Province, Ling equipped the full insignia of a governor to escort him and had a man convey word to Wei: "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning."

When Shou went on a mission to Liang and passed through Xu Province, Ling equipped the full insignia of a governor to escort him and had a man convey word to Wei: "Do not wonder at the many guards — it is the power of classical learning."
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 聘梁 is a diplomatic mission to Liang, not 'hire Liang'.
Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen heard of it.
Cui Xian's cousin by marriage Li Shen

To supply a worthy enemy with a talented man is not fitting."
To supply the enemy with a man of talent is not fitting."
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 英賢 is the talented man supplied; 寇敵 is the enemy. The literal reverses the roles.
Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint Zhan censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which Xian did not favor.
Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint Zhan censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to Zhan's liking.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 非其好也 refers to Zhan's preference, not Cui Xian's; the censor post was not what Zhan desired.
Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to remove [Zhan] as censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to Xian's liking.
Cui Xian was commandant of justice; he memorialized to appoint [Zhan] as censor — he was taken in for talent and reputation, which was not to his (Zhan's) liking.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 除 here means appoint, not remove; 非其好也 refers to Zhan, not Xian.
With Li Gai of Zhao Commandery he was a friend of no opposition.
With Li Gai of Zhao Commandery he was an intimate friend of complete accord.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 莫逆之友 means intimate friends in perfect accord; 'friend of no opposition' is an opaque calque.
He helped fix the Five Rites and awaited orders at the Wulin Hall.
He helped establish the Five Rites and awaited edicts at the Wenlin Hall.
文林館 is Wenlin Hall, consistent with the chapter, while 參定 and 待詔 mean helping establish the rites and awaiting edicts.
Ling's clansman Zhaoshi was grandson of Wei, vice director of the masters of writing Liang.
Ling's clansman Cui Zhaoshi was a grandson of Cui Liang, Vice Director of the Masters of Writing under Northern Wei.
魏 modifies the office held under Northern Wei, and 亮 is the clansman Cui Liang; the revision removes the false person named Wei.
When he reached the border of Qi Province, local bandits led by Cui Kumarajiva seized him.
When he reached the border of Qi Province, local bandits led by Cui Jiaye seized him and wanted to force him to join them.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 迦葉 is Jiaye (Kāśyapa), not Kumarajiva; idiomatic also omits 欲逼與同事.
When he reached the border of Qi Province he was captured by local bandits such as Cui Kumarajiva and others.
When he reached the border of Qi Province he was captured by local bandits such as Cui Jiaye and others, who wanted to force him to join them.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. Same wrong rendering of 迦葉 as Kumarajiva; literal also drops 欲逼與同事.
His son Kan, at the end of Wei also served as Unrestricted Regular Attendant and envoy on a mission to court Liang.
His son Kan, at the end of Wei also served as Unrestricted Regular Attendant and envoy on a mission to the Liang court.
The cited wording directly supports this correction. 'court Liang' reverses the modifier order of 聘梁.
His father Shitai was remonstrating and editing grand master.
His father Shitai was a Remonstrance Counselor.
諫議大夫 is the office Remonstrance Counselor; the previous wording invented editing and the proposal retained an unnecessary parenthesis.
